1.pericope_label: Now these are the names of the tribes. From the north end to the coast of the way of Hethlon, as one goeth to Hamath, Hazarenan, the border of Damascus northward, to the coast of Hamath; for these are his sides east and west; a portion for Dan. And by the border of Dan, from the east side unto the west side, a portion for Asher
debates: Whether the division is literal or spiritual
Why the order of the tribes differs from every earlier list
What the reserved portion may and may not be used for
outliers: Henry explains Dan being placed first and furthest from the sanctuary by that tribe having revolted
Gill reads each tribal name as naming a class of believer
Ellicott finds the Levites here levelled up to the priests in the size of their portion
themes: A land measured out in parallel bands
Stones in an arch wedging one another fast
A portion lifted off the top of the whole
Land that may never be sold

15.pericope_label: And the five thousand, that are left in the breadth over against the five and twenty thousand, shall be a profane place for the city, for dwelling, and for suburbs: and the city shall be in the midst thereof. And this shall be the measures thereof; the north side four thousand and five hundred, and the south side four thousand and five hundred, and on the east side four thousand and five hundred, and the west side four thousand and five hundred
debates: Whether the measures are reeds, rods or cubits
Whether the prince here is a magistrate or the Messiah
Whether the plan can be laid on real ground at all
outliers: Ellicott holds the arrangement geographically impossible even on the smallest cubit
Keil and Delitzsch treats one figure for the city as a copyist error marked by the Masoretes
Clarke finds no cultivated land between the Levites and the prince except on two sides
themes: A strip left over that is common and not holy
A city set exactly in the middle of its own square
A field too small to feed the town it serves
A map wider than the country it describes

23.pericope_label: As for the rest of the tribes, from the east side unto the west side, Benjamin shall have a portion. And by the border of Benjamin, from the east side unto the west side, Simeon shall have a portion. This is the land which ye shall divide by lot unto the tribes of Israel for inheritance
debates: Whether the southern tribes add anything to the northern pattern
Whether the names carry a moral sense
Where the southern boundary actually ran
outliers: Gill reads Simeon, Issachar, Zebulun and Gad each as a class of believer
Ellicott states that the southern five repeat the northern seven exactly
Clarke fixes Kadesh south of the Dead Sea at the extremity of Gad
themes: Five portions laid out like the seven before them
A tribe no longer scattered inside another
An inheritance drawn by lot but not of this world

30.pericope_label: And these are the goings out of the city on the north side, four thousand and five hundred measures. And the gates of the city shall be after the names of the tribes of Israel: three gates northward. It was round about eighteen thousand measures: and the name of the city from that day shall be, The Lord is there
debates: What unit the measures of the city are given in
Why Levi is counted a tribe here and Joseph only one
Whether the city named at the end is earthly or the church
outliers: The same figure is made thirty-four miles, five miles and thirty-two thousand miles by three voices
Henry notes that neither the city nor the land is called by its old name
Clarke would have left the closing name untranslated
themes: A number whose unit nobody can name
Twelve gates with twelve names written on them
Old names dropped from a familiar map
A city named for who lives in it
